previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, atrial fibrillation, prior CABG, and alcohol abuse was admitted for evaluation of shortness of breath, chest pain, and new right lower back pain. Initial labs showed a mild leukocytosis and thrombocytopenia, with a slightly elevated d-dimer, but troponins were negative and imaging showed no pulmonary embolism or acute cardiac event. The shortness of breath was determined to be at baseline, with a possible minor aspiration event suggested by lab changes and a patulous esophagus on CT, though no pneumonia or COPD exacerbation was confirmed. The back pain was attributed to a muscle strain. He remained in paroxysmal atrial flutter but asymptomatic, with no need for changes in management. He was discharged home on his prior medications with a short course of low-dose oxycodone for back pain and counseling on smoking cessation.

Brief Hospital Course:
MICU course:
___ male w/ history of atrial fibrillation not on warfarin, 
HTN, CAD s/p CABG, CVA, COPD not on home O2, and EtOH abuse who 
presents with chest pain found on arrival to be hypotensive with 
acute liver failure in setting of positive acetaminophen level 
and recent heavy alcohol use.

# Acute hepatitis / mild liver failure:  AST and ALT both >1000 
(AST peaked at 7200) with evidence of synthetic dysfunction as 
manifest by elevated INR. MELD 19 Likely from  acetaminophen 
ingestion as well as heavy alcohol use. His CMV IgM also 
returned positive. Given positive acetaminophen in context of 
significant transaminitis, through toxicology recommendations, 
the atient was placed on NAC 21-hr protocol and labs were 
closely monitored for any worsening signs of liver failure.  His 
LFTs, INR, tylenol level downtrended and he was transferred to 
the floor on ___, where his labs continued to improve.

# Chronic R headache: ongoing and was why has been taking 
regular tylenol.  evaluated by neuro in past (neg head CT), 
referred for occipital nerve injection. patients states was told 
he was not a candidate for this based on his anatomy, but did 
not follow up further. Has been taking ___ tylenol daily for 
these headaches for most of past year.  Now understands cannot 
continue to take this. Recommended referral back to neurology 
for outpatient follow-up.

# Hypotension, Tachycardia:  Hypotensive and tachycardic on 
admission that resolved after adminsitration of IVF and 
vanc/cefepime. We held diltiazem until hypotension resolved. He 
did require IVF boluses for tachycardia on standing 
intermittently, but these episodes were felt to more likely 
reflect deconditioning and possibly some autonomic dysfunction 
from chronic alcohol abuse. It was recommended that he wear 
thigh high TEDS. 

# Pneumonia: CT with worsening consolidation noted in RUL 
concerning for pneumonia. Given recent discharge on ___, 
patient was started on vancmycin and cefepime for HCAP on 
admission to the MICU. On transfer to the floor he was 
transitioned to levaquin and completed a ___tOH Abuse: Social work was consulted for his history of heavy 
abuse. Patient was monitored with CIWA protocol with lorazepam 
given that phenobarb contrainidcated in marked hepatic 
impairment. He was given MTV, thiamine, folate throughout 
hospital course. There was a question of hallucinosis but this 
resolved. He should be reconnected with his outpatient 
psychiatrist. Abstinence from alcohol was recommended.

# Refeeding syndrome: Patient required aggressive electrolyte 
repletion. 

# Anemia: Hct trended during this hospitalization, baseline low 
___. Low retic. Likely reflected some amount of marrow 
suppression from liver disease and ETOH, with low TIBC probably 
reflecting marrow suppression from inflammation. Ferritin level 
indicates adequate iron stores. Low suspicion for hemolysis. 
Stable this AM. Last ___ in ___ showed polyps, consider repeat 
as outpt to exclude colon cancer. 

# Line inflammation: Pt had difficulty with peripheral access 
and RIJ was maintained on the floor. On the day of discharge new 
trace fibrinous exudate was noted at the insertion site and the 
line was removed. There was no e/o cellulitis and no fevers. 
Site covered with DSD, abx ointment, and he was started on 
Keflex x5 days to prevent soft tissue infection.

# CAD s/p CABG: EKG w/o e/o MI. History of chronic chest pain at 
baseline. LVEF 60-65% in ___. Stable throughout hospital 
course. He was continued on ASA and rosuvastatin

# pAF: Not on coumadin. Had brief episode of RVR but otherwise 
was stable on home dilt, ASA. He did require IVF boluses for 
tachycardia on standing intermittently, but these episodes were 
felt to more likely reflect deconditioning and possibly some 
autonomic dysfunction from chronic alcohol abuse. It was 
recommended that he wear thigh high TEDS. 

# Hypothyroidism: Continued levothyroxine

# BPH: Initially held tamsulosin given hypotension. Once 
resolved, resumed his home medications. Continued finasteride.

# H/o esophagitis: His home PPI was continued.

INDICATION:  ___ male with chest pain. Evaluate for pneumothorax.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal chest radiographs were obtained with the patient in the
supine position.

COMPARISON:  CT from ___ and radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is a right central venous line that ends at the cavoatrial junction. The
heart size is normal, and the patient is status post median sternotomy. There
is bibasilar opacities reflecting fibrosis as noted on the dedicated chest CT.
There is no pleural effusion or pulmonary edema.

IMPRESSION: 

Pulmonary fibrosis including in the right upper lobe is better assessed on the
dedicated chest CT.

INDICATION:  ___ male with chest pain and abdominal pain. Evaluate for
pulmonary embolism or dissection.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial MDCT images were obtained through chest, abdomen and pelvis
following the administration of 130 cc of Omnipaque IV contrast material and
oral contrast material.  Sagittal and coronal reformatted images were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT from ___..

FINDINGS: 

The thyroid is unremarkable, and there is no supraclavicular lymph node
enlargement. The airways are patent to the subsegmental level.  There are
prominent mediastinal lymph nodes including a right 1.2 x 0.9 cm right
peritracheal lymph node and a prominent subcarinal lymph node, symmetry prior
exam. The heart, pericardium, and great vessels are within normal limits. 
There is a moderate hiatal hernia, and the esophagus is patulous and
fluid-filled, possibly predisposing the patient to aspiration.

Lung windows show emphysematous changes as well as fibrotic changes
predominate within the right lobe. There is no pleural effusion, focal
consolidation or pneumothorax.  Consolidation within the right upper lobe has
increased in size from ___, concerning for infection (6:30).

CTA: The aorta and main thoracic vessels are well opacified. The aorta
demonstrates normal caliber throughout the thorax without intramural hematoma
or dissection.  The pulmonary arteries are opacified to the segmental level.
There is no filling defect in the main, right, left, lobar or segmental
pulmonary arteries.

LIVER: The liver enhances homogeneously with no focal lesions. The portal and
hepatic veins are patent, and there is no intra or extrahepatic biliary duct
dilatation.

GALLBLADDER: The gallbladder is unremarkable and contains radiopaque
gallstones.

SPLEEN: The spleen is normal in size and shape.

PANCREAS: The pancreas enhances homogeneously without ductal dilation or
peripancreatic fat stranding.

ADRENALS: The adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

KIDNEYS: The kidneys are normal in size and shape.  There are bilateral renal
cysts, and smaller bilateral renal hypodensities are too small to characterize
but statistically likely to represent cysts. There is no hydronephrosis or
perinephric stranding.

BOWEL:  The stomach is mildly distended and unremarkable. The small bowel is
without obstruction or focal wall thickening.  The appendix is normal. The
large bowel contains feces without wall thickening or evidence of obstruction.
Sigmoid colonic diverticulosis is noted without evidence of diverticulitis. 
There is no intraperitoneal free air or free fluid.

LYMPH NODES: There are no pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal or
mesenteric lymph nodes by CT size criteria.

PELVIS: The bladder is decompressed with a Foley catheter in place. There is
no pelvic free fluid.. There are no pathologically enlarged pelvic sidewall or
inguinal lymph nodes by CT size criteria. The rectum is unremarkable.

VESSELS & SOFT TISSUE: There is extensiveatherosclerotic disease without
aneurysmal dilatation of the abdominal aorta. The aorta and its major branches
are patent. There are no hernias.

BONES: There are no suspicious lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions to suggest
malignancy.  The patient is status post median sternotomy.

IMPRESSION: 

1. Consolidation within the right upper lobe has increased in size from the ___, concerning for infection. Continued emphysematous changes and
pulmonary fibrosis.
2.  No evidence of pulmonary embolism or aortic dissection.
3.  Chronic findings of cholelithiasis, diverticulosis and atherosclerotic
disease.
